newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Corpgro slips on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Corpgro slips on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in South African acquisitive industrial group Corpgro Ltd slipped on Wednesday on profit-taking after improved earnings but were seen improving once the company consolidated its shares, dealers said.
"With the wealth of shares in issue at the moment, I think that after the good results the guys will probably be taking profits," one dealer said.
Corpro reported earnings per share for the six months to March 31 of 1.31 cents from 0.64 cents previously.
It also announced that it planned a nine-for-one share consolidation which would result in about 200 million shares in issue compared to its current 1.7 billion shares.
"I think it's the amount of shares that's bringing the share down. People are realising that these shares aren't going to move," one dealer said.
"Fewer shares will be a good thing for the stock," he added.

By 1343 GMT the Corpgro stock was trading down 12.12 percent or four cents at 29 cents. It was the second biggest percentage loser on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in a traded volume of more than three million shares.
